works.title: Thrasymachus: Justice Is the Interest of the Stronger
works.source: The Republic, Book I — Benjamin Jowett translation
works.note: Thrasymachus hurls down the challenge the whole dialogue must answer: that justice is merely whatever serves the powerful.

works.title: The Ring of Gyges
works.source: The Republic, Book II — Benjamin Jowett translation
works.note: Glaucon's thought experiment: would any man stay just if a ring made him invisible and unaccountable?

works.title: Until Philosophers Are Kings
works.source: The Republic, Book V — Benjamin Jowett translation
works.note: The "third wave" Socrates fears to utter: that no city will know rest until power and wisdom meet in the same hands.

works.title: The Good and the Sun
works.source: The Republic, Book VI — Benjamin Jowett translation
works.note: The Form of the Good is to the mind what the sun is to the eye — the source of both truth and the power to know it.

works.title: The Allegory of the Cave
works.source: The Republic, Book VII — Benjamin Jowett translation
works.note: The most famous passage in philosophy: prisoners chained before shadows, and the pain — and danger — of being turned toward the light.

works.title: The Myth of Er: The Choice of Lives
works.source: The Republic, Book X — Benjamin Jowett translation
works.note: The Republic closes with the soul choosing its next life after death — and the verdict that the blame is the chooser’s, never God’s.
